subtitle: Multirole aircraft · historical research dossier
introduction: Follow the visible aircraft, the organizations behind the program, and the public record linking specific observed examples. Source assertions, direct observations and unresolved questions are identified individually below.
scope: Major-system and institutional research across the cited dates. This is a conceptual overview, not an engineering teardown, complete parts list or present-day production census. People are shown only in their dated public roles.

systems.title: Airframe and wings
systems.text: The Army ODIN reference describes a central fuselage and straight, high-mounted wings. These labels identify external form; neither the illustration nor this description establishes internal structure or materials.

evidence.reference: General information / external configuration description; search-index access.

systems.title: Twin-boom tail
systems.text: Two tail booms and an elevated horizontal tail surface distinguish the external layout. DIA used the tail as one feature in its comparison of Iranian and recovered examples.

evidence.reference: External tail configuration.
Printed page 7: tail comparison.

systems.title: Wheeled undercarriage
systems.text: Wheeled landing gear is visible in the examples compared by DIA. The record supports this observable category, not a specification for every production configuration.

evidence.reference: Printed page 7: landing-gear comparison.

systems.title: Observation equipment
systems.text: DIA identifies externally visible surveillance equipment in its comparison. Contemporary launch coverage also describes electro-optical observation equipment. The available observations do not identify all internal devices or establish uniformity across batches.

evidence.reference: Printed page 7: surveillance equipment.
Description of observation equipment in launch reporting.

systems.title: Ground segment
systems.text: Janes' illustrated deployment reporting shows a separate control vehicle alongside the aircraft. The ground segment is therefore presented as its own system category, without suggesting that its hardware sits inside the airframe.

evidence.reference: Image and description of the accompanying control vehicle.

timeline.title: The first-unveiling date remains disputed
timeline.text: Janes gives April 2016; the Army ODIN entry gives April 2017. The reviewed material does not resolve the discrepancy, so neither year is treated as settled.

evidence.reference: Unveiling date in program background.
Unveiling date in reference background.

timeline.title: Production-line inauguration reported
timeline.text: Mehr's contemporaneous gallery reports a Mohajer-6 production-line opening in Tehran on February 5, 2018. This anchors the announced production milestone; it does not measure actual output.

evidence.reference: Gallery introduction: inauguration, date and city.

timeline.title: Recovered aircraft enters the public evidence record
timeline.text: DIA compared a largely intact aircraft recovered from the Black Sea in 2022 with examples pictured in Iran and Iraq, judging their visible features indistinguishable. This is an attributed identification of particular examples.

evidence.reference: Printed page 7; report information cutoff October 27, 2022.

timeline.title: U.S. assessment and Iranian account differ
timeline.text: AP's account of the DIA briefing records the U.S. assessment of Iranian supply to Russia and Iran's position that a small number had been supplied before the invasion, with further supply denied. These positions remain separately attributed.

evidence.reference: London briefing and account of Iran's stated position; search-index text.

timeline.title: DIA expands its evidence presentation
timeline.text: DIA announced an updated report in August 2023 using recovered material and declassified imagery. Its coverage spans multiple aircraft families; an observation about one model cannot automatically populate another model's record.

evidence.reference: Announcement of expanded report and its evidentiary scope.

organizations.title: Qods Aviation Industries
organizations.text: Treasury attributes Mohajer-6 design and manufacture to QAI and records the Light Airplanes Design and Manufacturing Industries alias from mid-2020. The attribution is explicit; it is not a factory inspection.

evidence.reference: QAI identity and manufacturer attribution.

organizations.title: Iran Aviation Industries Organization
organizations.text: Treasury places QAI under Iran Aviation Industries Organization (IAIO), within the defense ministry structure. This is institutional oversight, not a component supply relationship. IAIO should not be confused with the similarly abbreviated Aerospace Industries Organization.

evidence.reference: QAI subsidiary and IAIO/MODAFL relationship.

organizations.title: Ministry of Defense and Armed Forces Logistics
organizations.text: MODAFL is the ministry named in Treasury's organizational account. A ministry's oversight does not establish which premises, workers or subcontractors produced an individual aircraft.

evidence.reference: Institutional placement of QAI and IAIO.

organizations.title: HESA: a sibling is not a proven manufacturer here
organizations.text: Treasury identifies QAI and HESA within IAIO's wider aviation organization. Shared institutional ownership alone does not establish that HESA assembled Mohajer-6; no such product edge is added.

evidence.reference: IAIO, QAI and HESA organization description.

people.title: Amir Hatami
people.text: Iranian defense minister at the reported production-line inauguration. Mehr identifies him as the official opening the line; that ceremonial role does not establish personal engineering authorship.

evidence.reference: Named official at the inauguration.

people.title: Mohammad Pakpour
people.text: IRGC Ground Forces commander identified in contemporary reporting as attending the inauguration. Attendance is public-event context, not proof of factory management.

evidence.reference: Officials attending the Tehran ceremony.

people.title: Seyed Hojatollah Ghoreishi
people.text: QAI board chairman in Treasury's dated leadership record. Current officeholding and individual design responsibilities are not asserted.

evidence.reference: QAI leadership: chairman.

people.title: Ghassem Damavandian
people.text: QAI managing director and board member in Treasury's record. Its October release uses the spelling Ghasem; this is a name variant, not another manufacturer.

evidence.reference: QAI leadership: managing director.
Ghasem Damavandian name spelling.

people.title: Other named QAI board members
people.text: Treasury lists Hamidreza Sharifi-Tehrani, Reza Khaki, Majid Reza Niyazi-Angili and Vali Arlanizadeh as board members. These are historical organizational roles, not a list of product engineers.

evidence.reference: Four further QAI directors.

people.title: Afshin Khajeh Fard
people.text: Treasury names him as IAIO's chief in May 2024. The documented relationship is leadership of the parent organization; product-specific technical work is not established.

evidence.reference: IAIO leadership identification.

manufacturing.title: Tehran: a historical production event
manufacturing.text: Mehr places the 2018 line-opening ceremony in Tehran. The exact premises, surveyed location and later operating status are unresolved. A corporate address is not substituted for a verified product factory, and no map coordinate is assigned.

evidence.reference: City and inauguration event; no precise premises established.

manufacturing.title: Manufacturer attribution has a narrower meaning
manufacturing.text: Treasury's QAI attribution does not describe internal workshare, supplier contracts, batch allocations or an exclusive final-assembly line. The network records the attributed organization while leaving facility fields empty.

evidence.reference: Manufacturer attribution; no batch-level factory allocation supplied.

assessment.title: An observed aircraft is not an entire production series
assessment.text: DIA's comparison supports an origin assessment for the pictured examples. It cannot establish a complete inventory, every variant, or continuity of production. Its October 2022 information cutoff also predates the Shahed-238 display.

evidence.reference: Report scope, cutoff and Mohajer-6 visual comparison.

assessment.title: Source dates and current status are different
assessment.text: The 2018 event report and subsequent institutional records describe different moments. They do not establish that the same line remains active today. The dossier preserves those dates instead of presenting a live factory or personnel registry.

evidence.reference: Historical inauguration only.
Dated organizational record.

subtitle: Jet-powered one-way aircraft · historical research dossier
introduction: Examine the public display, attributed development organization and evolving identification record. Exhibition configurations and later Russian derivative reporting remain separately scoped throughout this dossier.
scope: Exterior and major-system categories only. Displayed options are not a unified production configuration, and Russian Geran-3 findings are not an Iranian Shahed-238 parts list. Leadership and venue records are dated institutional context.

systems.title: Delta-wing airframe
systems.text: The 2023 display imagery shows a delta-wing exterior in a matte dark finish. An observed finish is not evidence of a particular coating technology or verified performance.

evidence.reference: Original analysis of exhibition imagery and visible finish.

systems.title: Jet propulsion
systems.text: The November display analysis identifies the named Shahed-238 as jet-powered. This supports the broad propulsion category; no engine model, construction detail or performance figure is inferred here.

evidence.reference: Named Shahed-238 identification and broad jet-propulsion category.

systems.title: Flight-management systems
systems.text: Public analysis discusses differing avionics configurations, but the exhibition did not establish one verified internal arrangement for all aircraft. This card represents a system category, not a located assembly or shared production design.

evidence.reference: Configuration discussion and explicit uncertainty about implementation and maturity.

systems.title: Displayed configuration options
systems.text: Three examples were displayed. The reviewed analysis leaves their testing, availability and configuration maturity uncertain. They must not be combined into a single aircraft containing every announced option.

evidence.reference: Three displayed examples and uncertainty about fielding.

timeline.title: An unnamed jet aircraft appears on film
timeline.text: Janes examined footage from a documentary premiered on September 26, 2023. The aircraft was unnamed in the trailer; the footage is a precursor observation, not a verified Shahed-238 naming date.

evidence.reference: Documentary premiere and unnamed aircraft.

timeline.title: Named public display in Tehran
timeline.text: The War Zone identifies the November 19 exhibition as the public Shahed-238 display. Tasnim independently records the exhibition visit and Tehran venue. A public display establishes visibility, not serial-production output.

evidence.reference: Shahed-238 public display identification.
Exhibition date and venue.

timeline.title: Early identification was not immediately confirmed
timeline.text: UNN interviewed forensic-institute director Oleksandr Ruvin, who said his institute's research had not established Shahed-238 use at that point. This dated absence of confirmation does not disprove later observations.

evidence.reference: Direct interview with Oleksandr Ruvin about the institute's findings at that date.

timeline.title: A Russian derivative needs its own evidence scope
timeline.text: UNN reports Ukrainian intelligence's examination of a Russian Geran-3 U-series sample. Its relationship to Shahed-238 does not make the sample's internals, suppliers or manufacturing arrangements evidence for the Iranian aircraft.

evidence.reference: Russian sample identity and distinction from Iranian design.

timeline.title: Civilian-impact investigation
timeline.text: Human Rights Watch identifies a Shahed-238 in a February 28, 2026 Dubai hotel-forecourt incident and relays local authorities' report of four injuries. The investigation concerns civilian harm, not manufacturing attribution; HRW could not rule out military guests at the hotel.

evidence.reference: Dubai hotel investigation, aircraft identification and limits.

organizations.title: Shahed Aviation Industries Research Center
organizations.text: CSIS attributes Shahed-238 development to Shahed Aviation Industries. This is a research assessment, not a manufacturer declaration or final-assembly inspection, so the supply-network development edge is conservatively marked inferred.

evidence.reference: Development attribution to Shahed Aviation Industries.

organizations.title: IRGC Aerospace Force
organizations.text: Treasury described SAIRC as subordinate to the IRGC Aerospace Force in November 2022. That institutional record predates Shahed-238's named display and cannot independently establish this model's manufacturer workshare.

evidence.reference: Shahed Aviation Industries Research Center institutional description.

organizations.title: Ashura Aerospace University
organizations.text: Tasnim identifies the university in Tehran as the exhibition venue. Its presence in the public record is as a host location; no Shahed-238 manufacturing relationship is established.

evidence.reference: Location of the IRGC Aerospace Force exhibition.

people.title: Ali Khamenei
people.text: Tasnim records his visit to the exhibition as supreme leader and commander-in-chief in November 2023. This entry describes that dated public role, not product engineering authorship or present officeholding.

evidence.reference: Exhibition visitor and public role at the event.

people.title: Amir Ali Hajizadeh
people.text: Treasury identifies Hajizadeh as IRGC Aerospace Force commander in 2019; Janes identifies him in that role in the 2023 documentary. Neither record establishes that he personally designed Shahed-238.

evidence.reference: Dated command role.
Documentary interview participant and command role.

people.title: Saeed Aghajani
people.text: Treasury names Aghajani as IRGC Aerospace Force UAV Command commander in October 2021. This provides earlier institutional context; no product-specific Shahed-238 development role is established.

evidence.reference: Dated UAV Command leadership identification.

people.title: Product-specific engineers remain unverified
people.text: The reviewed development assessment names an organization, not a verified engineering team. Public commanders and exhibition attendees should not be converted into designer or supplier records.

evidence.reference: Organizational development attribution without individual engineering credits.

manufacturing.title: A Tehran exhibition venue is not a factory
manufacturing.text: The November 2023 venue establishes where the aircraft was shown. It supplies no proof of final assembly there. No military-site coordinates or factory marker are assigned.

evidence.reference: Exhibition venue only.

manufacturing.title: Iranian final assembly remains unresolved
manufacturing.text: The reviewed CSIS profile does not provide independently verified, product-specific Iranian final-assembly premises or workshare. General Shahed-family manufacturing statements are insufficient to fill that gap.

evidence.reference: Development/manufacturing discussion lacks independently verified Iranian site allocation.

manufacturing.title: Geran-3 observations stay with the Russian sample
manufacturing.text: The reported Geran-3 examination concerns a distinct Russian sample. Transferring its plant, companies or hardware findings to every Iranian Shahed-238 would erase the very provenance distinctions this collection preserves.

evidence.reference: Russian sample examination and separate production context.

assessment.title: Shahed is a family name, not a shared parts list
assessment.text: Treasury's 2022 family-level account predates the named Shahed-238 display. It supports institutional background only. Shahed-131, Shahed-136 and Geran-2 claims therefore do not automatically become Shahed-238 dependencies.

evidence.reference: Earlier Shahed-family scope.
Named Shahed-238 display in November 2023.

assessment.title: Identification changed as evidence accumulated
assessment.text: The January 2024 interview records uncertainty at one institute at one time. Later Russian-sample reporting and HRW's 2026 identification concern different observations; none retroactively verifies every earlier claim.

evidence.reference: Dated lack of institute confirmation.
Later Russian sample report.
Separate 2026 incident identification.

subtitle: U.S. one-way aircraft · industry and public-program dossier
introduction: Explore the aircraft's visible form, its attributed U.S. developer and manufacturer, and the organizations that funded, evaluated and fielded the program. The dated record follows the June 2025 project-funding announcement through broader task-force developments announced in August 2026.
scope: Conceptual exterior and major-system overview with high-level weapons-role context. This is not an engineering teardown or a complete supplier census. Test examples, fielded aircraft and related target platforms retain their own evidence boundaries; people appear only in dated public roles.

systems.title: External airframe
systems.text: Pentagon showcase reporting describes delta wings and a rounded nose, while noting that prototype features could change. The exterior establishes neither internal assemblies nor materials.

evidence.reference: LUCAS display paragraphs: delta wings, rounded nose and prototype-change caveat.

systems.title: Propulsion exterior
systems.text: CENTCOM's November photographs show an aft propeller. This visible feature supports a propulsion category, not a verified engine model or component manufacturer.

evidence.reference: Official photographs 251123-D-D0477-1163 and 251123-D-D0477-1029: externally visible aft propeller.

systems.title: Guidance and control
systems.text: CENTCOM describes autonomous operation at a broad level. The Senate's later public exchange did not disclose the internal implementation. This topic therefore shows a system category without locating avionics or asserting a specific decision-making architecture.

evidence.reference: Broad autonomy description.
Printed page 60: Marks declines to discuss LUCAS internals in the open hearing.

systems.title: Weapons and payload role
systems.text: LUCAS is described as a one-way attack aircraft. Yuma's December evaluation report specifically describes inert payloads and a weapons payload still under development in that test context. Later fielding does not make that test configuration a universal weapons specification.

evidence.reference: Opening paragraphs: one-way role, inert evaluation payloads and dated development status.

systems.title: Ground and launch support
systems.text: The Navy's reported shipboard demonstration establishes a support segment outside the aircraft. The visual treats this as a separate topic, without suggesting that a ship, launcher or control station is an internal aircraft component.

evidence.reference: Shipboard demonstration and Task Force 59 participation.

timeline.title: A documented production-transition investment
timeline.text: The official FY2025 APFIT list assigns $30 million to the Marine Corps LUCAS project. This is project-level funding, not a unit price, delivery count or identified company contract.

evidence.reference: FY2025 funded-project list: Low-cost Uncrewed Combat Attack Systems, $30 million, U.S. Marine Corps.

timeline.title: Pentagon public showcase
timeline.text: Official metadata dates the Pentagon tour to July 16; National Defense identifies LUCAS among the prototypes. A display establishes visibility, not completed fleet certification.

evidence.reference: Photo caption and event date.
LUCAS among the displayed prototypes.

timeline.title: A joint innovation framework
timeline.text: CENTCOM established the Rapid Employment Joint Task Force on September 23. This announcement describes the innovation framework; LUCAS and Scorpion Strike enter its public record later.

evidence.reference: Release 20250923-01: establishment date and organizational purpose.

timeline.title: The squadron enters the official record
timeline.text: CENTCOM announced Task Force Scorpion Strike on December 3. The accompanying LUCAS photographs carry November 23 dates; photograph dates and announcement dates describe different events.

evidence.reference: Release date and photograph captions.

timeline.title: Yuma evaluation disclosed
timeline.text: The Army published its Yuma evaluation account separately from the squadron announcement. The two reports do not establish identical configurations.

evidence.reference: Dated evaluation account; separate source scope from the squadron announcement.

timeline.title: First reported naval demonstration
timeline.text: The Navy reported its first LUCAS launch from a naval vessel on December 16 aboard USS Santa Barbara. The report was published two days later.

evidence.reference: Event date, named vessel and page publication date.

timeline.title: First combat-use announcement
timeline.text: CENTCOM reported that Scorpion Strike used one-way drones in combat for the first time during Operation Epic Fury. The release does not specify their configuration; the Senate subsequently identified LUCAS in its account of that milestone.

evidence.reference: Final paragraphs: task force's first combat use.
Printed page 5: chairman's LUCAS identification.

timeline.title: The wider task-force program evolves
timeline.text: CENTCOM announced plans for multinational Task Force Falcon Strike, drawing on Scorpion Strike's experience. The announcement expands the institutional story; it does not identify new LUCAS manufacturers or confirm aircraft transfers to particular partner countries.

evidence.reference: Falcon Strike announcement, consultation status and Scorpion Strike background.

organizations.title: SpektreWorks
organizations.text: National Defense names SpektreWorks as developer. The Arizona company's own description covers unmanned-systems engineering and production, without identifying individual LUCAS engineering workshare.

evidence.reference: LUCAS developer attribution.
Company self-description.

organizations.title: U.S. Marine Corps
organizations.text: Yuma's report identifies Marine Corps sponsorship of the evaluated aircraft. It does not assign the service manufacturing workshare.

evidence.reference: Opening program description: Marine Corps sponsorship.

organizations.title: Research & Engineering and APFIT
organizations.text: Research & Engineering's APFIT program supports transition into production. Its June announcement explicitly includes LUCAS, connecting public funding to the industrial story without identifying a component supplier.

evidence.reference: Program ownership, production-transition purpose and FY2025 LUCAS project listing.

organizations.title: CENTCOM and SOCCENT
organizations.text: SOCCENT personnel led the squadron effort introduced by CENTCOM. These command roles are separate from manufacturing.

evidence.reference: Task Force Scorpion Strike and SOCCENT personnel.

organizations.title: NAVCENT / Fifth Fleet and Task Force 59
organizations.text: The Navy identifies Task Force 59 as the naval organization that conducted the demonstration, within NAVCENT/Fifth Fleet. Its involvement records an operator and demonstration partner, not an aircraft assembler.

evidence.reference: Task Force 59 and NAVCENT organizational attribution.

people.title: Pete Hegseth and Emil Michael
people.text: The official July 16 caption identifies Hegseth as defense secretary and Michael as under secretary for research and engineering during the showcase tour. These are dated public leadership roles, not individual engineering credits.

evidence.reference: Named officials and roles in the event caption.

people.title: Dan Ermer
people.text: National Defense identifies Ermer as mission-capabilities director for rapid prototyping and experimentation. His direct comments describe early affordability constraints, not individual engineering authorship.

evidence.reference: Direct emailed comments and public official's title.

people.title: Nicholas Law
people.text: Yuma identifies Colonel Law as the research-and-engineering office's experimentation director, commenting on evaluation and production aspirations.

evidence.reference: Named experimentation official and quoted role.

people.title: Brad Cooper
people.text: CENTCOM names Admiral Cooper as its commander in the squadron announcement. The entry records command sponsorship, not personal authorship of the aircraft.

evidence.reference: Named command role in the announcement.

people.title: Curt Renshaw
people.text: The naval release identifies Vice Admiral Renshaw as NAVCENT/Fifth Fleet commander commenting on the demonstration. His public role does not establish industrial design responsibility.

evidence.reference: Named NAVCENT/Fifth Fleet commander.

people.title: Steven M. Marks
people.text: The Senate's official witness list identifies Major General Marks as director of the Defense Autonomous Warfare Group. His hearing appearance provides public oversight context; it does not establish that his organization supplied LUCAS hardware.

evidence.reference: Official witness name, organization and hearing date.

manufacturing.title: Whole-aircraft manufacturing attribution
manufacturing.text: Reuters identifies SpektreWorks as manufacturer and reports that it held manufacturing contracts; the company declined comment. The app records that explicit attribution without presenting it as an independently inspected production line.

evidence.reference: Opening attribution and Rapid Deployment section.

manufacturing.title: Reported government design ownership
manufacturing.text: Reuters reports government ownership of the LUCAS design intellectual property. This could permit other manufacturers; it does not prove that an additional named firm produced a delivered aircraft, or establish the terms of a license.

evidence.reference: Design intellectual-property ownership and multiple-manufacturer possibility.

manufacturing.title: Multiple producers were an objective
manufacturing.text: Yuma describes an intention to enable multiple manufacturers, without naming additional producers or verifying output. This remains an aspiration.

evidence.reference: Law's multiple-manufacturer aspiration.

manufacturing.title: Yuma is an evaluation venue
manufacturing.text: The Army establishes testing at Yuma, without assigning airframe manufacture there. Consequently the installation receives no supplier-factory edge.

evidence.reference: Evaluation venue and source scope.

manufacturing.title: Arizona corporate context
manufacturing.text: SpektreWorks describes itself as Phoenix-based. A city-level company description does not locate a LUCAS final-assembly line. Exact premises, audited production capacity and batch-level facility allocation remain unverified in the reviewed record.

evidence.reference: Corporate self-description, without a product-specific plant allocation.

manufacturing.title: Company capabilities are not a parts list
manufacturing.text: SpektreWorks advertises mechanical, electrical, software and flight services. That business-wide capability menu does not identify what was installed in a delivered LUCAS aircraft or establish a contract with any specific component company.

evidence.reference: Company-wide service categories; no LUCAS configuration attribution.

assessment.title: FLM 136 remains a separate catalog platform
assessment.text: SpektreWorks markets FLM 136 for threat emulation and counter-drone testing. Its catalog specification is not labeled as a verified fielded LUCAS configuration. Shared ancestry or resemblance therefore does not justify transferring its technical parts or performance figures.

evidence.reference: FLM 136 identity and threat-emulation scope.

assessment.title: Shahed-136 lineage is not a supply relationship
assessment.text: The Senate chairman describes LUCAS as derived through reverse engineering of Shahed-136. That historical attribution concerns Shahed-136, not Shahed-238, and does not establish an Iranian company as a supplier to the U.S. program.

evidence.reference: Printed page 5: explicitly names Shahed-136.

assessment.title: Public questions did not disclose the internals
assessment.text: Senator Mark Kelly asked about LUCAS decision-making and oversight. Marks offered a classified briefing instead of public technical detail. The unanswered questions must not be treated as confirmation of a particular autonomous weapons architecture.

evidence.reference: Printed pages 60–62: question, response and oversight discussion.

assessment.title: Wider drone targets are not LUCAS orders
assessment.text: The Senate distinguishes the Drone Dominance effort for smaller aircraft from broader autonomous-warfare work. Aggregate program ambitions cannot be converted into LUCAS purchase quantities, current inventory or SpektreWorks production totals.

evidence.reference: Printed pages 4–5: distinct program scopes.

assessment.title: An allied relationship remains unestablished
assessment.text: In a written answer, UK minister Luke Pollard said the department held no records of formal LUCAS engagement with U.S. counterparts or SpektreWorks. This dated records statement supports leaving a UK program edge absent; it does not rule out all informal contact or later change.

evidence.reference: Printed page 39, answer 118990.

assessment.title: A larger task force does not identify every aircraft
assessment.text: The August Falcon Strike announcement discusses a wider mix of aerial and maritime systems and planned partner participation. It does not establish that every task-force activity uses LUCAS or identify new LUCAS factories, subcontractors or export customers.

evidence.reference: Multi-domain scope and invitation process; no product-specific manufacturer census.

edges.title: Attributed manufacturer
edges.text: Reuters attributes whole-aircraft manufacture to SpektreWorks. The edge does not identify subcontractors or production premises.

evidence.reference: Manufacturer and manufacturing-contract attribution.

edges.title: Evaluation sponsor
edges.text: The Army identifies Marine Corps sponsorship of the evaluated aircraft, without assigning manufacturing workshare.

evidence.reference: Opening program description.

edges.title: Hosted evaluation
edges.text: Yuma's documented role is evaluation; it is not presented as a supplier factory.

evidence.reference: Evaluation venue.

edges.title: Led task-force effort
edges.text: CENTCOM identifies SOCCENT personnel as leading Scorpion Strike's squadron-building effort.

evidence.reference: Final paragraph: SOCCENT role.

edges.title: Fielded squadron
edges.text: CENTCOM identifies LUCAS aircraft with Scorpion Strike's announced squadron. Fielding is not manufacture.

evidence.reference: Squadron aircraft identification.

edges.title: Conducted naval demonstration
edges.text: The Navy identifies Task Force 59 as the demonstration operator, without assigning industrial supply responsibility.

evidence.reference: Task Force 59 demonstration role.

edges.title: Attributed developer
edges.text: National Defense explicitly identifies SpektreWorks as LUCAS developer. This documents a second industrial role, not another supplier.

evidence.reference: Firsthand showcase report: LUCAS developer attribution.

edges.title: FY2025 project funding
edges.text: APFIT lists $30 million for the Marine Corps LUCAS project. No company payment or manufacturing allocation is established.

evidence.reference: FY2025 project list: LUCAS allocation and Marine Corps association.

edges.title: Administers funding program
edges.text: The June release identifies APFIT as a Research & Engineering program supporting production transition.

evidence.reference: Opening paragraphs: office's APFIT program and transition into production.

edges.title: Established innovation task force
edges.text: CENTCOM announced REJTF's establishment on September 23, led by its chief technology officer.

evidence.reference: Opening paragraphs: establishment and organizational leadership.

edges.title: Aligns with capability focus
edges.text: Scorpion Strike's squadron effort aligns with REJTF's capability work. Alignment does not establish a subordinate command relationship.

evidence.reference: Final paragraph: explicitly stated REJTF capability-focus alignment.

edges.title: Established task force
edges.text: CENTCOM announced the creation of Scorpion Strike, which had established a LUCAS squadron.

evidence.reference: Opening task-force announcement and squadron identification.

edges.title: Special-operations component
edges.text: CENTCOM's official directory lists SOCCENT among its component commands. This reviewed relationship has no inferred founding date.

evidence.reference: Component Commands introduction and SOCCENT listing.

edges.title: Maritime component
edges.text: The Navy identifies NAVCENT/Fifth Fleet as CENTCOM's maritime component.

evidence.reference: Closing NAVCENT/C5F organizational description.

edges.title: Established unmanned-systems task force
edges.text: NAVCENT established Task Force 59 in September 2021. This institutional origin predates its documented LUCAS demonstration.

evidence.reference: Opening announcement and TF59 commissioning caption.
